name: mangos-protocol-socket-checkpoint-and-restore
instr:
Applications should be able to persist protocol-owned socket state and later resume it as an ordinary disconnected mangos socket. Checkpoints must be portable across socket destruction without retaining transport resources. Restored behavior should match normal protocol behavior after fresh peers attach.

Checkpointing is atomic: success transfers a complete, deterministic snapshot, while any busy, concurrent, close, or capture failure preserves the original socket and message ownership unchanged. The versioned envelope identifies its protocol, rejects malformed or unsupported data with `ErrInvalidCheckpoint`, and never exposes partial results. `RestoreSocket` dispatches recognized identities without consuming its `SocketCheckpoint`; unknown or package-mismatched identities return `ErrCheckpointProtocol`, and live endpoints return `ErrCheckpointBusy`. Independent restorations never alias, and restored sockets support normal options, reconnection, close, and repeated checkpoint cycles. BUS, PAIRv1, SUB, STAR, PUB, PUSH, and PULL checkpoints preserve their logical queues and protocol metadata while excluding pipes, topology, hooks, and pipe affinity. Restoration preserves subscriptions, pruning, queue bounds, TTL, monogamous admission, best-effort delivery, message order and isolation, and exactly-once ownership wherever those properties apply. Cooked headers and forbidden send or receive directions remain identical to ordinary sockets, including PAIRv1 routing-header concealme
